summary:
# NOTES: *Dorothy* by Evelyn Raymond (1907, Platt & Peck; Gutenberg #40300)

Single book, no separate BOOK headings. Chapters I–XVIII.

## Cast
- **John Chester** ("Johnnie," "father John"): postman, Brown Street, Baltimore. Whistles on route. Later diagnosed with locomotor ataxia; hospitalized at Johns Hopkins; sent to country.
- **Martha Chester** ("Martha," "mother Martha"): John's wife, tidy housekeeper. Pins "Dorothy C." card; finds baby.
- **Dorothy C. (Dorothy Chester)**: foundling, found on Chesters' marble step on a spring morning, age ~12-13 at main action ("baker's dozen"). Brown eyes, curly yellow/brown hair, pretty figure, vain of small feet/hands. Wrinkles nose when perplexed. Miss Georgia = her teacher, vice principal.
- **Mrs. Betty Cecil Somerset-Calvert** ("Mrs. Cecil," "Miss Betty"): old Maryland widow-type, proud, gossipy, lives at **Bellevieu** (eagle-gate with bronze eagles on stone pillars). Poodle. Two Great Dane dogs: **Peter and Ponce**. Summer home in Hudson highlands: **Deerhurst**.
- **Ephraim**: half-deaf gray-haired coachman, fat bays.
- **Dinah**: ancient Black body-servant to Mrs. Cecil, dialect speech, rheumatism.
- **Methuselah Bonaparte Washington** ("Brown"): Ephraim's grandchild, small boy.
- **Mabel Bruce**: plump, greedy, frank, Dorothy's chum; daughter of plumber **Mr. Bruce** and **Mrs. Bruce** (Brown Street). Gets measles.
- **Mr. Lathrop**: postal colleague, friend of John; helps Dorothy at post office; later accompanies Chesters to country.
- **Postmaster** (unnamed "head man of all"): rejects Dorothy's request to take father's route.
- **"John Smith"** (lawyer, office on North Howard Street, top floor, 3 flights): fake lawyer, villain. Tall, light hair, left eye squints, eyebrows meet, glib. Former clerk of Kidder & Kidder who listened at keyhole; wrote letters; kidnaps Dorothy. Cause: monthly $10 letters paid by Mrs. Cecil (anonymous).
- **Aunt Chloe Chester**: John's old aunt who raised him; gloomy.
- **Mrs. Bruce's** relative: **Jane Jones** (Mrs. Jones, "sister") and husband **Bill Jones**, country-woman, become tenants of No. 77 at $20/month.
- **Jim Barlow**: shock-headed (almost white hair), very blue eyes, thin, orphan, barefoot farm boy; "Pshaw!" catchphrase; ambition to learn; reads from spelling book; "right vs wrong" morality.
- **Miranda Stott** ("Mrs. Denim," "Mirandy"): gruff truck-farm woman near Baltimore (~12 miles), four mules, schooner-shaped wagon, can't read. Serves her son (sick, "him," Smith) whom she loves most.
- **Tige**: her mastiff.
- **Daniel St. John**: elderly white-haired preacher, green goggles, gig with old mare **Nan**; hymns ("Bringing in the Sheaves," "Throw Out the Life Line"); cottage "Old St. John's."
- **Detective** (unnamed, "gentleman in business suit"); **Kidder & Kidder** (old attorneys, elder Mr. Kidder ~80, son).
- **Jehu**: hackman.

## Chronology
1. **Ch. I**: Spring morning; Martha screams at baby-wagon on step; card: "My name is Dorothy C. I have come to be your daughter." John laughs, goes to route. Mrs. Cecil stops John, asks about baby. Dinah breakfast scene. Dorothy spills milk, nearly chokes with bonnet strings. Pinned note (misspelled): "thee child Is wun Yere an too Munths old hur burthDay is aPrill Furst... with Ten doLurs" signed "dorothy's Gardeen hur X mark." John notes same person wrote both (odd r's, y's). Martha: "_she's mine_!"
2. **Ch. II**: Dorothy (12) scrubs front steps, Friday holiday. John confesses: "_I--am--doomed!_" Ataxia diagnosis (5 doctors). Dorothy takes ride on his route. Martha learns: "ataxy locomotor." At Bellevieu, Dorothy hands mail to Mrs. Cecil ("Johnnie" is a joke-friend). Mrs. Cecil scolds about illegal mail carrying; plans to send Chesters on vacation and invite Dorothy. Great Danes knock Dorothy down, stun her. Mrs. Cecil apologizes-ish. John gone.
3. **Ch. III**: Chester house empty; storm; Dorothy runs barefoot to Johns Hopkins (neighbor said ambulance took John). Grocer boy misdirects ("dead-set"). Dorothy faints at feet of statue "Christ the Healer" in entrance hall. Children's ward nurse (blue gown). Doctor (interne) with spectacles. Dorothy sleeps; Martha arrives.
4. **Ch. IV**: John has chance of recovery; to country later. Dorothy buys white slitted shoes ($1.97) and stockings with Martha's permission (max $2 shoes, $0.25 stockings). Shoes hurt; she rides car, gets stared at. Stranger ("man") at steps offers "great fortune."
5. **Ch. V**: Sunday. Dorothy sends roses to John. Mabel Bruce visits; eats most ham and pie; Dorothy breaks a tumbler. Dorothy announces "heiress." Mabel reveals family moving. Man (Smith) appears; Dorothy sends Mabel home.
6. **Ch. VI**: Martha home; plans move to Hudson-highlands farm (Hudson River, New York; old bachelor uncle's property, "rocky hill-farm"). Dorothy sees mother cry. Monday: Dorothy sent to post office for $10 money-letter (envelope, no registration). Dorothy spins happily Sunday night. Martha has presentiment; "that familiar summons was never again to be heard."
7. **Ch. VII**: Post office, Mr. Lathrop helps. Dorothy asks postmaster for John's beat; refused (advice: never keep secrets from mother). Smith (John Smith) takes her to his office; she writes note to Martha enclosing money-letter envelope; he leaves "to find messenger"; gone whole day.
8. **Ch. VIII**: Martha alone; Mrs. Bruce and sister-in-law Jane Jones arrive; offer to rent No. 77 for $20. Martha weeps. Mrs. Bruce brings dinner, Mandy cleans. Visit to John at hospital; he says "Do whatever you think best." Lathrop and detective come; Martha shows Dorothy's photo (curly hair, brown eyes).
9. **Ch. IX**: Dorothy locked in Smith's top-floor flat (three rooms, nailed windows, spiked shutters). Smith returns with milk, sandwiches; hackman Jehu takes her. She sleeps in coupé; wakes at truck farm with Miranda Stott, Jim, and bacon. Warnings: "Drink no milk."
10. **Ch. X**: Mrs. Jones fetches Mabel; Mabel describes caller (Tall, light hair, left eye squints, eyebrows meet, glib). Detective notebook. Lathrop plans trip Thursday. Martha leaves house Wednesday night, sleeps at boarding house across from Hospital. Morning: John insists on Dorothy; Lathrop lies; John speaks harshly to Martha ("you're deceiving me"). Newspaper headline: "FATE OF POSTMAN JOHN CHESTER'S DAUGHTER DOROTHY STILL UNKNOWN." John arrives at hilltop farm.
11. **Ch. XI**: Dorothy tries to escape; meets Jim (Jim Barlow; orphan; works for Mirandy). Jim reveals previous boy ("'Tother") drugged with white powders in milk; Smith took him away. Dorothy picks berries; homesick; Jim promises to watch. Dorothy in attic.
12. **Ch. XII**: Dorothy catches measles (from Smith—later revealed; she gave to him). Mrs. Stott nurses with sage tea. Dorothy kisses Miranda's hand. Jim taught words "baker," "tinker." Smith hiding in cottage upstairs; "It's _him_... They're goin' hard."
13. **Ch. XIII**: Mrs. Cecil ill then recovered; plumber Mr. Bruce at Bellevieu checking pipes; tells of Dorothy missing, $100 reward; Mrs. Cecil horrified, goes to Kidder & Kidder (lawyers); $500 reward advertised.
14. **Ch. XIV**: Jim reads newspaper ad ($500) in fire-kindling paper; Dorothy reads "DOROTHY"; Smith is sick with measles in cottage; Dorothy & Jim eat berries, talk; Dorothy learns Smith is "_hern_" (Miranda's son). Miranda locks Dorothy in harness room, sets Tige to watch.
15. **Ch. XV**: Jim decides to flee with Dorothy at night; drugs Tige's milk with powders; rags on Dorothy's feet; they walk through lanes; thorn lodged in Dorothy's foot; Jim pulls it out; she faints; storm; "We got to go back!" Dorothy kneels in prayer.
16. **Ch. XVI**: Dorothy refuses to return; Jim carries her piggyback; they rest under honeysuckle hedge; sleep. Constable/horse-jockey man questions them; then Daniel St. John (old preacher) rescues Dorothy, gives breakfast, bandages foot, cottage home; Jim and Dorothy leave with warnings the men are pursuing.
17. **Ch. XVII**: Mrs. Cecil, restless, drives out on Sunday in defiance of Dinah; sees hedge; "Drive! Kill the horses—save those children!" Rescues Dorothy and Jim; takes them to Bellevieu; Dorothy: "John Chester and his wife have gone to the country."
18. **Ch. XVIII**: Mr. Kidder reports that Smith (former clerk, discharged) is ill; will be exiled or imprisoned. Jim to be tested as Mrs. Cecil's protégé/gardener at Deerhurst. Crowd of Brown Street residents at Bellevieu; Dinah addresses them. Dorothy visits Brown Street but won't stop at No. 77. Journey by Hudson steamer to Cornwall; arrival at **Skyrie** (stone cottage on rock, vines); John in wheeled chair on threshold; Martha runs to her. "THE END" — continues in "Dorothy at Skyrie."

## Key Places
Brown Street (No. 77, one-hundred-block); Bellevieu (Mrs. Cecil); Johns Hopkins Hospital (Broadway, Christ the Healer statue); post office; Howard Street office (North Howard, top floor); Lexington Market; Kidder & Kidder (Baltimore Street); Deerhurst (Hudson highlands); Skyrie (hilltop farm, Cornwall NY); Miranda's truck farm (~12 mi from Baltimore); St. John's cottage; Peabody Institute; Towson; Union Station.

## Key Quotes
- "Dorothy's Gardeen hur X mark."
- "_she's mine_!" (Martha)
- "_I--am--doomed!_" (John)
- "Drink no milk." (warning note)
- "Stay quiet where you are..." (note to Dorothy)
- "FIVE HUNDRED DOLLARS REWARD!"
- "Pshaw!" (Jim)
